fit.gap_handling_summary: The CV makes good use of real accessibility, React, Storybook, booking-site and project API experience without manufacturing professional backend work or two years of experience. It preserves WCAG 2.1 rather than claiming WCAG 2.2 AA, and distinguishes unit testing from unproven end-to-end testing. Security, health-data privacy, production backend ownership and performance remain substantive gaps; the letter could more clearly express a willingness to learn the privacy requirements.

issues: The yoga website is described in both Experience and Selected Projects with substantial repetition.
The teaching-assistant institution is asserted without source support.
Project ordering is neither consistently chronological nor explicitly labelled as relevance-based.
The education date wraps onto a separate line in the PDF, making that entry less tidy than the others.

reasons: Single-column text extracts in a sensible order with intact words and standard headings.
Core React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Jest, Next.js and Storybook terms are present.
HTML5 and Firebase Authentication cover the corresponding general keywords; public API consumption provides a semantic match for third-party integrations.
Professional dates and junior positioning do not satisfy a strict two-year React/TypeScript experience filter.
Missing end-to-end testing, privacy, security and infrastructure terms reflect real evidence gaps rather than opportunities to insert unsupported keywords.

issues: The letter exceeds the explicitly requested limit of under 250 words.
It remains primarily a technical experience summary rather than a noticeably personal letter.
The candidate's authentic screen-reader-friend story was available but omitted.
The phrases about accessible React and project-based full-stack experience recur in the opening, motivation paragraph and closing.
It does not explicitly address willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements.
strengths: Correct company, role and Patient Experience team.
Connects documented accessibility work to the company's patient-first and privacy-by-default principles.
Uses specific evidence, including 20+ components and the Lighthouse score of 100.
Consistently identifies full-stack experience as project-based.
Does not reuse the earlier letter's obsolete student status or internship application.

spacing_issues: The CV is visually front-loaded: page one is dense while page two has substantial unused space below Volunteering.
The Selected Projects section continues on page two without a repeated section heading.
consistency_issues: Experience dates are bold and inline, while project dates are italic and right-aligned; this is workable but introduces an additional date style.
The education date wraps beneath the institution instead of following the cleaner date placement used elsewhere.
issues: The long teaching-assistant heading is crowded on one line.
The letter uses readable paragraphs and a matching serif typeface, but the technical middle paragraph is dense.

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'My accessible React internship' is an awkward compression; 'My internship work on accessible React interfaces' would be clearer.
'Other: Web accessibility:' uses a redundant nested label.
'accessible React and project-based full-stack experience' is repeated enough to make the letter feel formulaic.

notes_facts_used: Teaching-assistant experience in a first-year web-development lab.
One semester in spring 2025 helping approximately 30 students.
Second place in a 2024 student hackathon, with a three-person team building a transit delay notifier in 24 hours; candidate owned the frontend.
Volunteer social-media work for a sea swimming club.
Backend experience is limited to personal projects, reflected in the repeated project-based qualification.
misused: The teaching-assistant role is attributed to Liffey Institute of Technology although the notes give no institution.

requests.request: Please make the cover letter warmer and more personal, and keep it under 250 words.
requests.evidence: “particularly resonates with me” and “I would be delighted” provide some warmth, but the final letter still exceeds 250 words and devotes most of its text to technical experience.
requests.note: There is some personal reflection on accessibility, but no strong personal detail. The tool's reply only says the documents are ready and does not explain the missed length constraint.

evaluation.summary: The CV presents the candidate's real junior-level fit well, particularly accessibility, React, Storybook and project-based Node.js/PostgreSQL work, without inflating professional experience. Almost all factual content is supported, but the teaching-assistant institution is an unsupported addition. Both PDFs are readable and ATS-friendly, although the CV repeats the yoga project and is unevenly balanced across two pages. The main failure is request compliance: the cover letter remains over 250 words and only mildly personal despite having an authentic accessibility story available.
